library.label: Library
library.title: Create your first card
library.intro: A deck groups concepts. A concept holds what you want to learn, and each practice item asks you a question.

steps.1: In My decks, open New deck. Give it a name, such as Travel, and select Create deck.
steps.2: In My concepts, open New concept. Use “borrow” as the title and “take and return later” as the summary. Select Create concept.
steps.3: Open the concept and find New item. Choose Basic recall, enter “Take and return later” and “borrow”, then select Create item.
steps.4: Open the Travel deck. Under Add concepts, find “borrow” and select Add to deck.

library.tip: A concept can belong to several decks and share its progress. Use Show archived to find and restore content.

study.label: Review
study.title: How to review a card
study.intro: Today shows how many cards you can practise. Lexora uses your answer to plan when each card will appear again.

steps.1: Select Start session on Today when you have cards available.
steps.2: Choose the decks you want to practise and select Create session.
steps.3: Try to remember the answer, then select Reveal answer.
steps.4: Choose how well you remembered. Wait for Lexora to save the review before closing.

study.tip: To take a break, select Pause session. On Today, select View open sessions to resume.

import.label: Import
import.title: How to import cards
import.intro: Bring in Anki cards or use Lexora’s template to prepare a vocabulary, grammar or phrase set.

steps.1: Decide where you want to put the cards. You can create a deck while importing.
steps.2: Open Import to view the template or copy a prompt for ChatGPT. Upload the file or paste the generated text.
steps.3: Use the preview to check the front, back and tags of each card.
steps.4: Choose the deck and what to do with duplicates. Check the summary and select Import into the course.

import.tip: The preview lets you check columns and rows before saving. You can skip duplicates or copy them as new concepts.

progress.label: Progress
progress.title: See what you have practised
progress.intro: Statistics summarises your saved reviews. History shows them one by one.

steps.1: Open Statistics and select the period you want to see.
steps.2: Open History to filter by date, deck or rating.
steps.3: Return to Today to see whether more cards are available.

progress.tip: If you have no activity yet, review one card and wait for it to save.

preferences.label: Settings
preferences.title: Study at your own pace
preferences.intro: Choose how much to practise and how Lexora looks.

steps.1: In Settings, choose your language, theme and time zone. The time zone sets when your study day begins.
steps.2: Change the new card limit or the maximum reviews and save your preferences.
steps.3: To put Lexora on your home screen, use Install Lexora if it appears or open your browser menu.

preferences.tip: If you reach your limit today, you can carry on when the next study day begins.

data.label: Data
data.title: Download your data
data.intro: You can download your courses, content and saved activity, including archived items.

steps.1: In Settings, find Keep your data with you.
steps.2: Choose Download CSV for a spreadsheet or Download JSON to keep the data in a structured format.
steps.3: Keep the file somewhere private. The download contains your data in plain text.

data.tip: Use the export to keep a copy of your data. Lexora does not restore it automatically.

Metadata.title: Lexora
Metadata.description: Study languages with your own decks, practice cards and spaced repetition.

Home.tagline: From knowing it to saying it.
Home.description: Turn your vocabulary, grammar and notes into language flashcards. Lexora schedules your reviews so the things you practise stick.

example.title: Try a flashcard
example.instruction: Say the phrase in English, then check your answer.

practice.title: From your notes to your next review

organize.title: Organize what you study
organize.body: Create a course for each language and group your cards by topic. Add cards by hand or import your notes from a file.

practice.title: Put your memory to work
practice.body: Recognize words, recall them without hints or complete sentences. Use free study whenever you want to revisit a topic.

review.title: Review when it matters
review.body: Spaced repetition adjusts when each card comes back based on how you answer.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.intro: Lexora is a JVOR Studios project. Find out what data the service uses and how you can manage it.

purpose.title: Your account and study activity
purpose.body: We use your email to identify your account and send confirmation or recovery messages. We store your courses, cards, preferences and history to provide the service and schedule reviews. Technical logs help protect accounts and diagnose errors. Session cookies keep you signed in. Your browser may also remember your language and theme preferences.

providers.title: Services Lexora uses
providers.body: Vercel hosts the website and Supabase manages accounts and the database. If you choose Google, we use the basic identity information you authorize to sign you in.

retention.title: Retention and deletion
retention.body: Your courses, preferences and history are kept while you have an account. Lexora stores import results and diagnostics and removes your active data when you delete your account. Operational backups follow their own retention cycle. Downloads you save stay under your control.

rights.title: Your options and rights
rights.body: In Settings you can update your information, download a copy or delete your account. You can also request access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection or portability where applicable, and lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency.

Terms.title: Terms of service
Terms.intro: Lexora is a free web app by JVOR Studios for studying languages with your own flashcards. These terms explain what Lexora offers and the rules for using it.

service.title: What Lexora offers
service.body: You can create courses and organize flashcards into decks. You can add cards by hand or import your own material. Lexora schedules reviews based on your answers. You can also practice freely and see your study history and statistics.

account.title: Your account
account.body: You need an account to save your study material and progress. You can create a new account with Google. If you already have a password account, you can still use it to sign in. Use your own account and protect your credentials.

materials.title: Material you add
materials.body: You keep any rights you have in the material you add. When you upload it, you allow Lexora to store and use it so you can study and manage your data. Only add material you have the right to use, and respect other people's rights and privacy.

use.title: Acceptable use
use.body: Use Lexora lawfully. Accessing other people's accounts, sending harmful files or interfering with the service is prohibited. Lexora may limit what an account can do to protect the service against abuse.

availability.title: Availability and changes
availability.body: You need an internet connection to study and sync your data. Maintenance or technical issues may interrupt the service. We will publish the current terms and their update date on this page. Your legal rights still apply.

data.title: Your data and closing your account
data.body: You can download a copy of your data or delete your account in Settings. If you want to keep your courses, decks and study history, download a copy before deleting your account. The Privacy Policy explains what data Lexora uses and how it is kept.

Import.title: Import
Import.intro: Import vocabulary, grammar or phrases for a topic. Review the cards and choose a deck before saving.

preparation.title: Import template
preparation.intro: Use one row per card. The front and back are required. Leave the third column empty if you do not use tags.
preparation.sampleUnavailable: You can generate a prompt for this language. Sample templates are available in English, French, German and Italian.
preparation.instructions: Customise the prompt and paste it into ChatGPT. Then upload the CSV or paste its contents below.
preparation.copied: Prompt copied. Paste it into ChatGPT.

prompt.goal: Create {count} level {level} {targetLanguage} flashcards about {topic} for import into Lexora.
prompt.vocabulary: Put a word or expression in {targetLanguage} on each front. Give its meaning and a natural example in {targetLanguage} on the back.
prompt.grammar: Put a question, gap-fill sentence or correction task in {targetLanguage} on each front. Give the solution and briefly explain the rule on the back. Cover the topic’s uses, forms, examples and common mistakes.
prompt.phrases: Put a useful phrase in {targetLanguage} on each front. Explain its meaning and when to use it on the back, with a short context where helpful.
prompt.coverage: Cover the most useful subtopics for this level. Avoid duplicate fronts and variations that test exactly the same thing.
prompt.language: Write the meaning or explanation on the back in {language}, keeping the examples and answers in {targetLanguage} where appropriate.
prompt.focus: Prioritise {focus} within the topic where it fits the format.
prompt.format: Return a comma-separated CSV in UTF-8. Use {directive} as the exact first line. Start the data on the second line, with no header row. Each data row must have exactly three fields. Write the front, back and tags in that order. Put double quotes around every field and double any double quotes inside a field.
prompt.fields: Use one card per line, with no blank lines or line breaks within fields. Limit the front to {front} characters and the back to {back}. Use plain text.
prompt.tags: Separate tags with spaces. Use :: for hierarchies, such as sports::equipment, and hyphens within names. If a card has no tags, keep the third column as an empty quoted field.
prompt.delivery: Provide a downloadable lexora.csv file if you can create it. Otherwise, return only a CSV code block with the complete contents, without extra text or Markdown tables.

DataInformation.title: Your data in Lexora
DataInformation.intro: This is a personal workspace with public registration closed. Here is what is stored, where it lives and what deletion means.

content.title: Content and history
content.body: Your profile, preferences, courses, cards and review history stay in your account until you change them or delete the account. Archiving hides content without destroying its relationships or history. Reviews are preserved during the life of the account.

imports.title: Imported files
imports.body: The original file is not stored on the server. Import records keep the filename, hash, mapping, counters and bounded error diagnostics for the life of the account. A diagnostic may include up to 500 characters from a row. They are private and deleted with the account.

exports.title: Downloads you control
exports.body: JSON and CSV backups are checked before download and stored unencrypted on your device. You can restore them to the same account with a recent session. After confirmation, the server stages the data and replaces the contents in one transaction. Pending card imports are stopped. Downloaded copies remain on your device after account deletion.

deletion.title: Deleting an account
deletion.body: Deletion requires your current password, explicit acknowledgment and a recent live Auth session. An enabled second factor must also be verified. The transaction removes the Auth identity and all its application data, including archived content, imports and review events. A failed transaction rolls back. Public registration remains closed afterwards.

providers.title: Where the app runs
providers.body: Supabase provides authentication and the PostgreSQL database. Vercel hosts and runs the web application. If you choose Google, your identity and basic profile are used to sign in through Supabase, without requesting Gmail or Drive permissions. No learning content is sent to an AI service. This personal delivery adds no content analytics, Sentry or new email provider.

limits.title: Backups and technical logs
limits.body: Account deletion removes active Auth and application records. Provider backups and technical logs follow the providers’ own retention policies; this action does not claim to erase them immediately. Application logs do not intentionally capture your passwords, card content or exported files.

Settings.title: Settings
Settings.intro: Make Lexora fit your rhythm. Your preferences are saved to your account and restored when you enter from another device.
Settings.timeZoneNote: Use an IANA name, such as Europe/Madrid. Daily allowances reset at midnight in this zone; changing it may change what is available today.
Settings.maximumReviewsNote: Leave empty for unlimited reviews. From 0 to 2,000; 0 pauses cards in Review.
Settings.limitsNote: From 0 to 100 new cards. Due learning steps remain available when an allowance is reached; lowering a limit does not undo saved reviews.
Settings.showIntervals: Show an estimate of the next interval after revealing the answer. You can toggle its visibility during the session.
Settings.courseNote: Switching course preserves its content and its own limits. Save any pending preference changes first.
